To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a compact CNN model for optical-flow computation can be obtained by: 1) processing the input images in a pyramid, and using a warping layer to propagate the flow estimate to the next level, 2) using a cost volume, and 3) processing it with a CNN.

(i) a compact model for optical flow can be designed by using a pyramid of CNN features, warping, a cost volume, and a simple architecture, (ii) a compact model is easier to train, and (iii) a compact model can achieve state-of-the-art performance on the MPI Sintelfinal pass and KITTIMonocular benchmarks.

a) a pyramidal CNN architecture that warps and processes cost volumes can achieve state-of-the-art results for optical flow estimation and b) it is possible to achieve these results with a small CNN model, trained end-to-end.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (i) We show that a simple and well-established approach for optical flow estimation, based on pyramids, warping, cost volumes, and CNNs, can outperform the recent FlowNet 2 model, which uses a much more complex architecture, and (ii) we demonstrate that the FlowNet 2 architecture is not a necessary requirement for achieving good results in optical flow estimation.
